a:r.a:t: Transport or Attachment to Phospholipids Requires Conversion to Fatty Acyl-CoA

p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting activation of a fatty acid by conversion to a fatty acyl-CoA. To the left, is the pyrophosphate molecule, where O- binds right to P, which bonds down to O-, double bonds up to O, and bonds right to O, which bonds to P. P bonds down to O-, right to O-, and double bonds up to O. An arrow, represented by inorganic pyrophosphatase (in blue), points down to 2Pi. Below this is a bracket, and the equation: Gamma G'[degree sign] = -19 kj/mol. A plus sign is to the right. To the right of this, the ATP molecule is at the top, where -O bonds right to P, which double bonds up to O, bonds down to O-, and right to O, which bonds to P. P double bonds up to O, bonds down to O-, and right to O, which bonds right to P. (A red arrow starts at this bond and points back to O.) P double bonds up to O, bonds down to O-, and right to O, which bonds right to adenosine (in a box). Below this is a fatty acid, where O- bonds down and left to C, which bonds left to R, and double bonds down and right to O (all in red). This is step 1: The carboxylate ion is adenylylated by ATP, to form a fatty acyladenylate and PPi. The PPi is immediately hydrolyzed to two molecules of Pi. Below the fatty acid molecule are reversible arrows, identified as fatty acyl-CoA synthetase (in blue) pointing to fatty acyl-adenylate (enzyme-bound) molecule. This begins with R, which bonds right to C, which double bonds down and right to O and bonds up and right to O (all in pink), which bonds right to P. P double bonds up to O, bonds down to O-, and right to O, which bonds right to adenosine (in a box). Below this, CoA-SH (highlighted and where S has two red dots above it) has a red arrow pointing back up to C. Below this are reversible arrows, represented as fatty acyl-CoA synthetase (in blue), and has an arrow darting right to AMP. This is step 2: The thiol group of coenzyme A attacks the acyl-adenylate (a mixed anhydride), displacing AMP and forming the thioester fatty acyl-CoA. Below the reversible arrows is the fatty acyl-CoA molecule, where O double bonds down and left to C, which bonds left to R (all in red), and bonds down and right to S-CoA (highlighted). This is all bracketed. Below the bracket is the equation: Delta G'[degree sign] - -15 kj/mol (for the two-step process).
